I have been growing cotton here in Quzhou for 35 years, so I know this land. My 13.1 mu is all cotton — that is what my family has always done, and the soil here suits it. With 6 mouths to feed and some family working off-farm, I need this crop to pay.

Last year I used Bt cotton seed from the dealer in town — the bollworm used to eat us alive before these seeds, so I will not go back. I buy the improved seed again, about 2 kg for my plot. Costs more but worth it.

For fertilizer, I do what has worked. Before planting I spread diammonium phosphate as base fertilizer, maybe 2 bags (50 kg each) across my land — that gives me phosphorus. Then I add urea as topdressing when the cotton starts flowering and bolls form, that is the important time. I think about 20 kg of nitrogen per mu total is right for cotton here — less and the bolls are small, more and the plant grows tall leaves but few bolls. Phosphorus maybe 8 kg per mu from the DAP. Potassium I add about 10 kg per mu — cotton needs potassium for strong bolls, my neighbor who skipped it had weak plants.

Cotton is thirsty but not like corn. I have well irrigation, so I water 4 times — after planting if dry, at squaring, at flowering, and at boll filling. Not more, electricity costs money.

Pesticide — even with Bt seed, I still spray for aphids, mites, and plant bugs. Usually 6-7 times through the season. I cannot lose bolls to bugs.

I plough deep before planting — cotton roots need to go down. Rotary is not enough for cotton in my experience.

If weather is good I expect around 250 kg seed cotton per mu. Some years better, some worse.
